content.thinking:
I'm planning the full file in one careful pass without testing in between, designing a cyborg medic character with a detailed skeleton—hips, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, articulated arms and legs—plus a staff prop, keeping the API usage safe and robust.

For colors I'm settling on white/graphite armor with a glowing teal-green accent, bronze skin, silver cyborg plating, and a cybernetic left half-face, aiming for an Overwatch-style clean look using flat colors and subtle gradient paints for panel shading. Now I'm working out the skeleton coordinates for a 1.8m standing A-pose figure facing forward.

Mapping the joint hierarchy: pelvis as root, then a spine chain running up through named segments to a chest tip, followed by a neck chain parented to the spine, and a head joint at the top, being careful with point counts matching span/name requirements for each chain.

I'm fine-tuning the vertical placement of these joints to hit a realistic head height around 1.8 units—adjusting pelvis, spine tip, neck, and head coordinates so the skull sits roughly centered near 1.68-1.7 with the crown topping out near 1.82 once hair or helmet geometry is added.

Now I'm setting up the leg chains: hips placed slightly apart at y=0.93, with ankles targeted near the ground. I'm defining the hip-knee-ankle IK chain with a forward bend direction, checking the reach distance stays within limits, then attaching a toe joint off the ankle for the foot.

Then I'm building the leg geometry by sweeping varying radii along the chain — thicker at the thigh, narrowing at the knee, widening slightly at the calf, and tapering at the ankle.

For the look, instead of a single color gradient down the leg, I'll keep the base tube as a dark graphite suit material and layer separate armor pieces on top — thigh plate, knee pad, shin guard, boots — positioned by sampling points along the chain.

I realize sweeping a larger-radius tube segment over a cropped range of the chain gives armor plates that naturally bend with the limb, which is much better than rigid cylinders. I'll use flat caps at the sweep boundaries to close off the plate edges cleanly.

Now I'm working out the skeleton proportions: hip joint at t=0, knee at t=0.5, foot tip at t=1, splitting each leg into thigh and shin segments of equal length, with the hip positioned near the pelvis at roughly y=0.93-0.95. For the arms, I'm placing shoulders outward at x=±0.22, y=1.42, giving the upper arm a length of 0.30 and the forearm 0.27, angled downward and outward about 30° from vertical for a natural A-pose.

Computing elbow and wrist...

For the pauldron, I'm scaling a flattened sphere with a ring trim and attaching it to the shoulder joint, offset slightly up and outward. For hands, I'm planning a palm box with finger joints forming digit chains.

I'll keep each hand simple—four fingers with two joints each plus a two-joint thumb, around ten joints per hand, which keeps the total joint count manageable. The right hand grips a vertical staff reaching the floor, designed like a healing caduceus with a glowing teal orb and wings at the head, positioned near the wrist.

For the fingers, I'm writing a helper function that computes curved finger chains by taking a base position, direction, and a set of curl angles per joint, so I can wrap them rigidly around the staff for the gripping hand while keeping the left hand relaxed and slightly curled.

Now I'm working out hand placement: for the left hand I'm setting a downward-and-forward orientation vector, and for the right hand gripping the staff I'm positioning the wrist along the staff line and figuring out its hand direction.

For the grip itself, I'm thinking through how a fist wraps around a vertical pole—fingers curling horizontally around it, palm against the back side, with the forearm bent forward so the fist sits in front of the body. I'm roughing out the shoulder and elbow joint positions to support that pose.

I'm working out the grip geometry: with the forearm roughly horizontal, the fingers need to curl around the vertical staff, stacked from index near the top to pinky near the bottom, each wrapping horizontally around the pole with knuckles positioned on the near side facing the body.

Working out the finger arc geometry...

I'm working out the palm box geometry relative to the wrist and pole position, trying to get the palm's depth and orientation right so the fingers attach at the correct front edge, and reasoning through which axis corresponds to palm width given the hand wraps around a vertical pole.

Now I'm figuring out the thumb's joint positions, treating it as a small two-joint rod that arcs around the pole from the base of the palm toward the front, using a similar angular parameterization as the fingers but with a different angle range.

The hand's tip joint is where the finger chains will attach, so I'm making sure the arm chain (shoulder, elbow, hand) has that tip properly defined for the fingers to parent to. For the left arm, I'm planning a relaxed hanging pose with slightly curled fingers, and considering giving it an exposed robotic/cyborg look.

Now I'm working out the geometry for the left hand's wrist and palm position, calculating the elbow and wrist coordinates from directional vectors and normalizing the arm segments to get accurate joint placements. I'm positioning the palm box oriented along the hand's direction vector to set up for finger placement.

Still working out finger curl rotation axes...

Still working out thumb placement and curl direction for the front-facing position, then I'll move on to wrapping the right hand fingers and sketching a prosthetic left forearm sweep.

For the head, I'm thinking of a half-cyborg design: skull sphere with a separate jaw, and stylized eyes done via decal -- a glowing teal iris on the organic eye and a glowing ring visor on the mechanical one, applied onto the skull surface.

Working out eye placement via azimuth and elevation hits on the sphere, with mirrored angles for left and right. Planning two eye textures: one natural warm amber iris, one cyber teal glow.

For the rest of the face I'm thinking small wedge for the nose, a decal for the mouth, brow strokes as thin slabs, and asymmetric ears -- a human ear on one side and a glowing cyber ear-piece on the other. For hair, I'm considering a swept-back cap built from a partial hemisphere geometry.

Now I'm fleshing out the hair color gradient from dark roots to teal tips, with extruded fringe swoops and a jointed ponytail chain trailing off a spike end. For head gear, I'm skipping a halo ring in favor of a small cyan headset ring with a boom mic, then moving into building the torso by lofting a white chest plate over a spine chain.

Writing loft stations...

For the chest emblem, I'll avoid logos and instead design a generic "heal core" decal — a circular glowing teal panel with a plus sign, placed as an emissive decal on the front of the chest armor loft, calculating the surface position via a ray hit against the chest mesh.

For the belt, instead of a risky lathe sweep, I'll just use a scaled cylinder part around the waist to approximate the ellipse shape, scaling it along one axis since lathe doesn't support non-uniform scale directly.

Now I'm working out the pelvis and leg proportions, then moving on to the tactical details: hip armor plates, utility pouches with teal trim, glowing green med-vial holsters, and a medic backpack with tank cylinders and indicator lights, possibly with small wing-like fins for an overwatch medic aesthetic.

For the fins I'm planning two angular stabilizer wings as extruded parts attached to the chest via hinge joints, kept solid white with teal edges and separate glowing slit details. For the neck I'm deciding between a swept tube with a lathed collar ring or a simple capsule rod between two points for the chain joint.

I need to bind capsule endpoints to the neck bone explicitly since they default to nearest joint, and pass a chain reference where a joint is expected. Then I'm setting up the collar as a small lathed cylinder near the neck, and moving on to sweeping the leg armor with radius arrays for the thigh guard.

Now I'm working out the knee location by solving the limb chain for its points and offsetting forward slightly for the knee pad, then keying radius arrays across the leg tube for the shin and thigh guard transitions.

Now I'm working out the boots and feet: the ankle joint gets a boot shape with a foot box sized roughly 0.26 long by 0.1 wide, plus a toe cap, trying to decide between a simple box foot or a swept capsule form for the boot upper.

I'm also placing the sole so it barely sinks below floor level, splitting it into a white top layer and a thin graphite sole layer, and figuring out where the ankle and toe joints sit vertically. Then I shift to the staff prop, planning to parent it to the right hand joint so it's held naturally and stands against the floor.

The staff itself gets its own design: a graphite shaft with white banding and grips, a ferrule cone touching the floor, and an ornate top with a torus ring, a glowing teal core sphere, winged blade extrusions, and spiraling teal coils around the head.

Adding a glowing ring around the orb and flanking wing blades, then working out the cyborg details on the left side—mechanical forearm with teal glowing lines, cyber eye, cheek plate, and a partial-sphere head panel.

Still defining plate geometry...

The eye decal placement on the plate works fine, so I'll shift the start angle a bit to avoid overlapping the nose area, keeping the eye comfortably within the plate's elevation range. For eyebrows, I'll skip painting them on the mixed skull/plate regions and instead add separate small rod elements positioned near the computed eye-surface hit points, offset upward slightly.

Placing brow rods right at the surface risks them sinking into the curved skull geometry, so I'm nudging each brow endpoint outward slightly along the surface normal to keep them visible above the skin.

For the nose I'll stick a small scaled sphere at the surface point, stretching it slightly to form a tip shape. The mouth will use a decal-style lip shape positioned lower on the face, and I'm planning a separate jaw piece as its own part.

I'm working out the skull and jaw geometry: a scaled sphere for the skull centered near the head point, then a smaller scaled sphere offset downward and forward for the jaw with its own joint and hinge position, down to where the neck joint connects.

Now I'm checking where the mouth decal would sit on the skull-jaw seam, calculating its approximate position using the skull's elevation angle, and confirming the jaw sphere's front edge extends past that point so the decal would be partially covered by the jaw bulge.

Given that, I think it's cleaner to anchor the mouth decal directly to the jaw part's own surface, using its center and an elevation offset so it inherits the jaw's rigging weights properly. I'm then considering where to place the nose decal on the skull's front surface.

Working out eye elevation and placement relative to the head center, then shifting to skin shading: defining a paint function that blends a shadow tone and base skin tone based on the surface normal's vertical component for a lit/shadow gradient. Now I'm setting up the hair cap as a scaled sphere offset from the head center with a partial angular range to leave the face open.

I'm adjusting the hair cap's theta angle to make sure its front edge sits above the brows rather than colliding with them, testing a few values until the geometry clears both brow and eye height, and considering tilting the cap backward so it still covers down to the ears.

Writing hair tuft curves...

Checking the ponytail position against the backpack geometry, I realize they'd overlap near the upper back, so I'm shortening the ponytail's path and adjusting its endpoint coordinates to clear the backpack's top edge.

For ears I'm giving the right side a natural skin ellipsoid while the left gets a cyber earpiece disc with a teal glow, plus a boom mic rod extending to the cheek. For the eyes I'm designing SVG textures — the right eye natural with an almond sclera, amber iris, and inked lid, the left eye cyber with a glowing teal iris featuring concentric rings and a crosshair, using alpha cutout so the surrounding skin shows through outside the eye shape.

Now I'm sketching the mouth SVG lip shape, deciding to skip cheek details, and thinking through the torso suit paint — a graphite base with teal piping, considering a thin vertical center line and possibly subtle noise-based panel variation.

Writing armor paint function...

Now I'm planning the shoulder pauldrons: a dome-shaped sphere scaled for the left shoulder in white, with a teal trim torus ring rotated flat around it, adjusting rotation to tilt the ring outward for a more dynamic silhouette.

For the arms, I'm sweeping a tube with tapering radii from shoulder to wrist, splitting the color so the upper sleeve is graphite suit material and the forearm switches to a silver prosthetic look right around the elbow joint.

For the right arm I'll do similar suit coloring with a white bracer on the forearm, while the left cyber arm gets glowing conduit rods placed along the forearm using points sampled from the arm chain.

Realizing the chain points sit at the tube's center, I need to offset the rod positions outward so they sit on the surface rather than inside it—computing offset points along a forward/side direction from each chain frame.

For the cyborg look, I'm planning a prosthetic hand with silver fingers and jointed segments, an exposed mechanical core near the left chest with shoulder implants, and a cybernetic left calf with piston rods and glowing accents replacing the suit there. Now I'm starting the actual code, setting up imports for the builder, IK limb helpers, and curve utilities before defining the geometry helpers.

Still writing imports and setting up the color palette -- white, graphite, teal accent with a silver and dark base, plus skin and hair tones.

Defining more paint functions...

Still building the skeleton...

Jaw hinge sits near ear height with the aim pointing forward-down, which works conventionally. For hair, I'm parenting the ponytail chain to the head. Now I'm setting up the leg loop, computing hip and foot positions symmetrically for left and right, then feeding lengths and a bend direction into the limb helper.

I'm checking that the hip-to-foot distance stays under the max reach so the knee bends naturally forward, then building each leg chain with named hip/knee/ankle joints and attaching a ball joint at the ankle tip for the foot.

Now I'm figuring out the foot geometry per side: a heel/body box roughly sized under the ankle, and considering whether to loft a boot-like shape with tapered stations for the foot body.

Still working out loft stations...

Adding the front sole block for the ball of the foot, checking the loft stations overlap cleanly with the sole height, and adding a trim torus around the ankle for the boot cuff.

I'm adding a graphite toe cap sphere, then sizing a white shin guard sweep with radii tapering from ankle to knee so it matches the leg tube's shrinking profile, and placing a knee sphere using the forward-projected knee point.

I'm checking the geometry: with hip-to-foot vertical span around 0.836 and leg segments of 0.46 each, the forward knee offset comes out suspiciously large (~0.192), suggesting the leg would bend more than intended — so I'm reconsidering whether the segment lengths need to be longer to keep the leg closer to straight.

Shortening the thigh and shin to about 0.425 each gives a total of 0.85, just over the 0.836 span, producing a small forward knee offset of roughly 0.077, which looks like a reasonable slight bend for a standing pose. I'm now adjusting the thigh armor's taper radii along its length to blend smoothly with the pelvis loft at the hip while narrowing toward the knee.

For the left leg specifically, I'm turning it into a mechanical prosthetic: swapping the shin's color to silver past the knee, adding piston details and a glowing core, and layering a thin teal ring sweep around the thigh at a radius just outside the armor surface for a decorative accent band.

I'm also simplifying the knee guard so the left side only gets a partial plate instead of full shin coverage, while the right leg keeps full armor from the knee down, then adding visible hydraulic rods along the back of the calf between the knee and ankle in a dark silver tone with a glowing teal ring highlight. Writing torso loft sections...

Checking the depth overlap between torso and armor loft at front and back to ensure the armor properly encloses the torso without clipping through it.

Now I'm adding decal details: a ray-projected emblem on the chest armor and a glowing teal circle with a plus sign for the core decal. Then I'm planning the abdominal pieces — a belt with a teal gem buckle, side pouches, and a row of small glowing vials standing across the front of the belt.

For the backpack, I'm designing a rounded box attached to the torso's rear with twin glowing teal tanks, vent grille textures on a back-facing plane, and starting to plan wing-like fin joints.

Writing fin geometry...

Setting the wing's extrusion direction as a horizontal vector angled outward and backward, with the up vector kept perpendicular so the thickness axis stays well-defined.

I also want a thin teal strip layered inside the white outline to create a glowing stripe effect, so I'm sketching a smaller inner polygon whose points fall within the white shape's bounds.

Checking that the teal shows through the white fine, then placing the wing/backpack joint near the chest, treating it as a hinge host in model space. Now I'm defining the arm points, with the right arm (s=-1) in a holding pose and the left (s=+1) relaxed, starting from shoulder and elbow coordinates.

Still computing elbow and wrist positions...

Computing finger joint positions using arc angles with radius offsets for sin/cos components, then checking tapering radii and naming conventions for the finger segment chains.

Now I'm working out the thumb placement, computing its base angle and position so it connects naturally to the palm's inner top edge, adjusting y-coordinates until the joint looks right. I'm also verifying the staff pole's center and radius line up with the sum of finger segment radii.

Adding the glove cuff next, then setting up the staff joint bone attached to the hand with an aim target pointing upward along the pole. I'm sketching out the staff's build: a tapered shaft rod from the base up to the top, plus wrapped sleeve sections and a darker grip wrap around the handhold area.

Now adding the ferrule spike tip touching the floor, teal collar rings at intervals along the shaft, white sleeve cylinders, and starting the capsule-like head shape at the top...

Shaping the wing blade outline...

Adding a spiral helix sweep around the staff shaft with a teal glow, tuned to three turns rising from mid-shaft up to just below the grip, and tagging all staff pieces with the staff bone before moving on to the left arm details.

Now I'm working out the prosthetic forearm geometry: a silver tapered sweep with varying radii along the limb, placing the elbow joint partway through the arm chain and defining the tube radii at each key point from shoulder to elbow to wrist.

I'm then setting up color rules for the sleeves and gloves -- the right arm gets a white armored bracer over graphite sleeve fabric with a dark glove on the hand, while the left hand stays silver to match the prosthetic.

Adding joint cap spheres at the elbows, white upper arm armor plating, and a small glowing teal cyber port near the left shoulder, plus a curved glowing line sweeping from the facial plate to the temple for the cybernetic head detailing.

Adding more hair tube sweeps...

Drawing the diagonal chest strap as a draped tube in dark teal, then adding hip tassets as small white boxes bone-weighted to the hips with slight rotation, plus a graphite codpiece box at the pelvis base.

I'm adding thin teal piping rods along the torso waist sides, rigging them to the chest bone since they move minimally, while attaching the lower hip pieces to the hip bone instead. Then I'm setting up the neck collar as a cylinder and the neck skin as a capsule, both weighted to the neck joint.

Writing part helper function...

Geometry factories give simple primitives like box, sphere, cylinder, and torus with low segment counts for a blocky look, plus scale and rotation options for positioning parts. Now I'm sketching out eye textures as SVGs within a small viewBox for the eye shapes.

Writing SVG clipPath code...

Adding crosshair details and glow effect, then moving to the mouth SVG with layered lip paths for depth and a center line stroke, before starting on the core decal shape.

Good, so aiming the plane toward -Z keeps the drawing unmirrored when viewed from behind, with default world up along +Y. For panel lines on the chest armor, I'm considering adding thin dark seam rods, but the positioning feels arbitrary—I'll likely skip most of these decorative details in favor of a simpler paint-based approach.

I'm building a nested paint function for the chest that layers seam coloring and teal accent stripes near the sternum on top of the base armor paint, taking advantage of how a Paint can resolve to another Paint during the bake process. Since this evaluates at rest pose during build time, the teal accents won't glow, which is fine for this piece—now moving on to the skull.

Writing decal placement code for the skull and plate surfaces, positioning eye decals using azimuth angles around the head center, while being careful about unused variable warnings under strict TypeScript settings.

Adding brow placement...

Now I'm placing a small nose bridge rod connecting to the nose sphere, using a flat skin tone color for simplicity. I'm double-checking the skull's vertical geometry near the jaw to make sure the nose sits correctly above it rather than overlapping.

Still working through mouth decal placement on the jaw surface...

I'm checking elevation 22 against the mouth point, but it's sitting too close under the nose with too little lower-face space, so I'm adjusting the jaw's vertical position lower to center around y=1.615 and rechecking where the mouth lands relative to the chin and neck geometry.

Checking the gap between mouth and nose base comes out to about 1.3cm, which works, so I'm sizing the mouth decal accordingly and moving on to verify eye, brow, and hairline placement for proportion -- raising the hairline slightly to 1.76 for a more natural chin-to-eye-to-hairline ratio, then confirming the hair cap's edge height clears everything with some tilt margin. Overall head width looks fine for a stylized look.

Now I'm adding jaw and neck geometry under the chin, then moving to headset details: placing silver earpieces on each side of the head with a small teal glow ring, and adding a partial torus arc over the top of the head connecting ear to ear, positioning it so the arc's peak sits around y=1.78.

Still working out band placement...

Now I'm sketching a thin mic boom curving from the earpiece down to the cheek with a small glowing tip, then setting up the hair cap as a partial sphere positioned and scaled over the head with a slight tilt.

For the hair material, I'm defining a gradient paint that blends dark plum tones with noise-based highlight bands near the crown. Then I realize the cap alone leaves the back of the skull exposed, so I'm adding a second hair piece sized and positioned to cover the rear of the head and avoid showing bare skin there.

Checking the geometry, I need to make sure this back-hair sphere doesn't bulge forward enough to cover the face or awkwardly swallow the ears — tuning its radius and offset so the front edge stays behind the eye line while still wrapping around the sides near where the ears sit.

Checking that the plate still shows over the hair at that z-offset confirms the layering works fine, and neither hair sphere interferes with the eyes. I'm placing the right ear with skin-colored geometry at a mirrored offset from the left, then noting I should add fingers in silver for the left hand next.

For the left hand, I'm working out where to position fingers for a hanging hand with the palm facing inward toward the thigh—since the palm normal points along x, the fingers line up side by side along the z axis instead, with the thumb positioned at the front-inner edge of the palm.

Still computing palm box orientation and finger placement offsets...

Writing the finger-chain helper...

I need arm.tip to use a non-null assertion since it's typed as possibly null, and I'm building a curl helper that bends a finger joint-by-joint by rotating a direction vector around an axis for each segment length. Now I'm moving on to constructing the leg meshes and joints.

Still writing sweeps and placement logic...

Adding belt trim glow, buckle with gem, and pouch placements...

Now I'm positioning glowing vials along the belt with graphite caps, then moving to hip tassets and stacked abdominal armor plates.

I'll place the backpack on the chest bone, then add two teal-silver cable rods curving from the backpack top up to the back of the neck as catmull sweeps. Both pauldrons will be white, with the left one getting an added cybernetic ring with a glow effect, and next I'll work on extruding the staff's wing-like top section.

Now I'm setting up the file imports and skeleton structure for the cyborg medic model, defining the builder, vector helper, and color constants before moving into the paint definitions.

Writing paint definitions...

Defining more paint functions...

Still defining limb color sweeps...

Laying out plate order along the arm, then shifting to the right bracer: white armor segments with a teal ring accent, upper arm guard proportions, and a sphere elbow pad positioned at the joint.

Now I'm fixing the exact joint coordinates for shoulder, elbow, and wrist on both arms so the chain of bones connects smoothly through rounded corners at each point.

Setting up the hand and finger bones to parent off the arm tip, with the staff joint attached to the right hand, then moving into the leg loop code to mirror left/right limb positions.

Writing leg loop code...

Adding the leg mechanics now, with piston rods connecting knee and ankle joints, a glowing calf ring, and a lofted foot shape bound to the ankle and ball joints.

Now I'm sanity-checking proportions: the pelvis crotch plate and hip joint spheres, where the thighs round into the pelvis, and the overall staff height relative to the character—roughly 1.88m against a 1.79m figure, which feels fine since staffs are often taller than their wielder. I'm also checking the grip height on the staff pole so it lands naturally near the hip or chest when held.

Setting up the staff joint, attaching it to the right hand, then building out its parts—shaft, grip, sleeve, and glowing teal ring bands using torus shapes for decorative accents...

Adjusting ring height, it's getting too tall overall, so I'm trimming the shaft and repositioning the ring center lower with a smaller radius to keep total staff height around 1.88.

Placing the orb glow sphere and halo ring just below the main ring, then setting up the paired wing layers to flank the staff symmetrically.

I'm skipping the tassel charms and emblem decal as extraneous, and planning the pack fins the same way as the other extrusions. I'm checking that the teal strip's extrude thickness is wider than the white outline so it peeks through both faces, then defining the wing joint parented to the chest joint with its position and direction vector.

I need to type the outline arrays properly—importing the `OutlinePoint` type so literal arrays infer as tuples instead of generic `number[][]`, and writing a scale helper that maps over outline points to resize and offset them while preserving the tuple type.

I'm double-checking that the spiral, bezier, and catmull helpers are all actually used in the model (hair tufts, mic, staff), then moving on to draping the chest armor surface over the torso using a catmull path, plus the collar and neck ring pieces. Now I'm placing the back grille panel and pack box geometry onto the chest joint bone with specific position offsets for the back face.

I'm positioning the twin tanks on the pack with teal glow cylinders and dark caps, sized and placed relative to the pack's top and bottom bounds, then adding a teal collar torus at the neck. Finally I'm raycasting against the armor skin to place a glowing core decal centered on the chest, checking it lines up with the existing paint seams and stripe pattern without clashing.

Now I'm defining the pauldron and shoulder plate geometry using partial spheres with custom phi/theta ranges, painted in metal, and working out the skull center offset to align the cyber plate against the head bone.

I'm verifying the plate's angular coverage runs from the front-left around to the left side, then checking whether the mic endpoint lands correctly on the jaw sphere's surface near the left edge.

For eyes, I'm skipping teeth as a decal detail and sizing the eye decals so they sit proportionally spaced on the smooth front of the skull, about 7.4cm apart. I'll skip adding a separate ear since the headset replaces it, then move on to writing the actual code.
